name: Ranganathaswamy Temple, Shivanasamudra
deity: Vishnu as Jaganmohana Ranganatha, the Madhya Ranga — the middle Ranga of the river — reclining upon the serpent Adisesha
period: Ancient, of Chola origins; enhanced by the Hoysalas, the Vijayanagara kings and the rulers of Mysore
summary: On a river-island beside the great falls of the Kaveri, Vishnu reclines as Jaganmohana Ranganatha — the Madhya Ranga, the middle of the three Rangas of the river. Ancient in origin and raised by the Hoysalas and Vijayanagara, it is the second stage of the pilgrimage of the five Ranganatha shrines.

sections.history: Shivanasamudra sits on an island of the Kaveri beside the famous falls where the river splits and plunges in twin cascades. Its temple to Vishnu as Ranganatha is honoured as the Madhya Ranga, the middle Ranga, standing between the Adi Ranga at Srirangapatna upstream and the Antya Ranga at Srirangam far below. The shrine is held to be very ancient, of Chola origins, and was enhanced over the centuries by the Hoysalas, the Vijayanagara emperors and the later rulers of Mysore.
sections.architecture: Built in the Dravidian manner, the temple gathers around the sanctum of the reclining lord, here worshipped as Jaganmohana Ranganatha, whose dark image is said to be carved from a single saligrama-like stone. Pillared halls and a gateway tower open before the shrine, and the island setting — ringed by the branching river and its falls — lends the temple a wild and elemental beauty rare among the great Vaishnava sanctuaries.
sections.legends: As the Madhya Ranga, Shivanasamudra is the middle jewel of the river's three Rangas, and the pilgrim who worships at Srirangapatna, Shivanasamudra and Srirangam in a single day completes the Triranga Darshana held to be of great merit. The lord here is honoured as the youthful, enchanting form of Ranganatha — Mohana Ranga — reclining in serene sleep upon the serpent while the Kaveri thunders past the island in its falls.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Vaishnava calendar — Vaikunta Ekadashi, the birth-star days of the lord, and the annual Brahmotsavam — with processions around the island shrine. The falls are fullest in the monsoon months, when the roar of the twin cascades joins the temple's festival, and the days of the Triranga pilgrimage bring devotees from across Karnataka.
sections.experience: Shivanasamudra joins the devotion of the reclining lord to the grandeur of the Kaveri's falls — an island shrine between two cascades, wild and quiet at once. It lies in the country between Mandya and Chamarajanagar, reached by road from Bengaluru and Mysuru, and it forms the middle stage of the Pancharanga pilgrimage that runs the length of the river.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; the monsoon falls season and the Brahmotsavam days are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Shivanasamudra lies on an island of the Kaveri beside its falls, reachable by road from Bengaluru and Mysuru; the nearest towns are Malavalli and Kollegal.
